query: Single-phase fcc FeCoNi has high saturation magnetization but a low coercive field, and reported single-phase fcc high-entropy alloys derived from it have coercive fields no greater than 100 Oe in the reported magnetic measurements. What single intervention could overcome this coercivity limitation? Formulate one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its mechanism, the predicted change relative to single-phase fcc FeCoNi or a matched derivative, the relevant compositional, structural, and measurement boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled experiment with an explicit falsification criterion.

generation.hypothesis: Introduction of a secondary phase or grain refinement in single-phase fcc FeCoNi will increase the coercive field by pinning domain walls or reducing magnetic domain size.
generation.intervention: Introduction of a secondary phase (e.g., carbides, oxides) or grain refinement (e.g., via mechanical alloying, annealing) to create a composite microstructure
generation.structural_mediator: Domain wall pinning or reduction of grain size to reduce magnetic domain size
generation.mechanism: Pinning of domain walls by secondary phase particles or reduction of grain size to reduce magnetic domain size, leading to increased coercive field
generation.predicted_outcome: Increased coercive field by at least 50% (to > 150 Oe) relative to single-phase fcc FeCoNi
generation.baseline: Single-phase fcc FeCoNi with a coercive field of 100 Oe
generation.boundary: FeCoNi-based high-entropy alloys with fcc structure and potential secondary phases or refined grain structure, measured at room temperature
generation.uncertainty: The effectiveness of the secondary phase or grain refinement may depend on factors such as particle size, distribution, and interface properties, which may require further optimization

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare single-phase fcc FeCoNi and a derivative with introduced secondary phase or refined grain structure, measure coercive fields using a vibrating sample magnetometer (VSM) or a superconducting quantum interference device (SQUID) magnetometer, and compare
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the coercive field of the modified sample is not significantly increased (> 100 Oe) compared to the single-phase fcc FeCoNi, the hypothesis is falsified
